objective: Add a lightweight repository-persistent project todo authority alongside existing fork-aware session todos and initiative work, exposed through one explicit scope-aware todo surface without introducing backlog promotion or duplicate initiative state.

in: Preserve current Pi session-branch todos and their fork/rewind semantics
Add a tracked repository-level .pi-todos.json authority for lightweight project todos
Add explicit session, project, initiative, and all todo scopes to the structured tool, slash command, completions, and docket
Keep active initiative work as a direct projection of pi-swe authority and route its mutations only through SweService
Provide atomic, locked, revision-checked, schema-validated project todo persistence
Add compatibility, concurrency, routing, UI, and documentation coverage
out: A backlog or promotion lifecycle between todo authorities
Automatic conversion or synchronization between session, project, and initiative todos
A database or event-sourced project todo store
Copying initiative work into project todo state
Automatic commits or pushes for project todo mutations
Changing initiative workflow.json layout or naming

constraints: Every todo item has exactly one canonical authority: Pi session entries, .pi-todos.json, or initiative workflow authority.
Existing unscoped standalone todo behavior remains session-scoped and backward compatible.
Project todos require explicit project scope; models must not create durable project todos merely as routine execution decomposition.
A focused active initiative remains the automatic execution view, while explicit session and project scopes remain accessible.
Project persistence must fail closed on malformed state, stale revisions, symlinks, lock conflicts, or ambiguous paths and must never silently reset data.
The tracked .pi-todos.json file contains only lightweight todo state and no initiative verification, evidence, or lifecycle data.
No database, second initiative ledger, implicit promotion, automatic commit, or push is introduced.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Existing session todos continue to reconstruct exclusively from the active Pi session branch and retain fork, rewind, hierarchy, ordering, blocking, and single-active-item behavior.
Project todos persist in a closed-schema tracked .pi-todos.json file across distinct Pi sessions and support lightweight create, move, delete, start, finish, block, unblock, and list operations.

Project todo writes use bounded validation, cooperative locking, revision/hash compare-and-swap, atomic replacement, and fail-closed recovery semantics under malformed, stale, symlinked, interrupted, and concurrent access.
The todo tool, slash command, completions, and docket expose explicit session, project, initiative, and all scopes with unambiguous authority labels, IDs, and per-item capabilities.

Automatic routing preserves current behavior: a focused active initiative projects initiative work; otherwise unscoped operations use session todos; project mutations always require explicit project scope.
Initiative todo operations continue to reread canonical workflow authority and route only through SweService, with no project-file copy or structural mutation bypass.
Documentation clearly distinguishes session, project, and initiative authority, persistence, Git behavior, routing defaults, and the absence of synchronization or promotion.
Focused tests, typecheck, repository checks, and the full test suite pass without regressions.

assessment.reason: The feature adds a new durable tracked authority and concurrent file mutation path while changing a shared command/tool/UI surface that already switches between session and initiative providers.
unknowns: The cleanest internal extraction for sharing lightweight todo rules between branch-event and snapshot persistence must preserve current characterization behavior.
The all-scope docket needs bounded rendering and deterministic mutation targeting without making implicit provider selection ambiguous.

practices.reason: Current session and initiative todo behavior must remain stable while scope-aware routing is introduced.
A tracked mutable JSON authority must resist stale writers, crashes, malformed input, symlinks, and concurrent Pi processes.
Session, project, and initiative items must share presentation without copying or synchronizing canonical state.
Explicit scopes, completions, labels, and the combined view must remain understandable and bounded.
Persistence, routing, and documentation require integrated regression evidence and explicit self-review.

obligations.text: Characterize and preserve session branch reconstruction, automatic provider routing, initiative projection, and unsupported workflow mutation behavior.
Test project todo schema, lifecycle, cross-session reload, atomic publication, stale revision rejection, lock contention, malformed files, symlinks, and injected interruption recovery.
Prove each item is read and mutated only through its owning backend, scope/ID mismatches fail closed, and no authority is copied or synchronized.
Test scope-aware command parsing, tool inputs, completions, authority labels, per-item capabilities, bounded all-scope rendering, and document the resulting contract.
Run focused todo and pi-swe tests, typecheck, repository checks, the full suite, and a source-bound model self-review of authority isolation, persistence safety, compatibility, and UX clarity.

work.title: Refactor todo authority contracts and add explicit scope-aware routing

testing.approach: Extend existing characterization and workflow-backend tests first for explicit session, project, initiative, and all routing while retaining current unscoped defaults, then refactor provider selection and contracts behind those tests.
testing.reason: The routing contract must be fixed before adding a third durable provider so compatibility failures are detected at the boundary.

work.title: Implement safe tracked project todo persistence and backend

testing.approach: Add schema, lifecycle, reload, fault-injection, stale-writer, concurrent-process, symlink, and malformed-state tests before implementing the .pi-todos.json snapshot store and project backend.
testing.reason: The new file is durable project authority and must fail closed rather than trade simplicity for silent loss or corruption.

work.title: Complete unified surfaces, documentation, review, and qualification

testing.approach: Add end-to-end tool, command, completion, and docket coverage for every scope and combined view; update documentation; perform source-bound self-review; then run focused and full repository verification.
testing.reason: The feature is complete only when all authorities are clearly accessible without ambiguous mutations and the existing pi-swe suite remains qualified.

evidence.summary: Source-bound model self-review of the current todo contract, scope router, project snapshot store/backend, workflow adapter, shared docket, tests, generated inventory, and operator documentation found no unresolved defects. Session operations remain branch-only; project operations are explicit and file-only; initiative mutations still reread authority and use SweService. Project persistence validates a closed bounded schema, rejects symlinks, malformed state, stale writers, and lock conflicts, and uses fsynced atomic replacement with interrupted-write cleanup. Unscoped compatibility, explicit scopes, qualified IDs, bounded combined rendering, per-item capabilities, and Git/no-promotion documentation are covered. This is a model self-review, not independent or human review.

decisions.text: Retain both session todos and repository-persistent project todos as separate lightweight authorities.
decisions.basis: The user explicitly requires both fork-aware temporary work and lightweight work that persists across Pi sessions.

decisions.text: Name the durable lightweight scope project rather than personal or backlog.
decisions.basis: The state represents project work but intentionally does not introduce a backlog or promotion lifecycle.

decisions.text: Store project todos in a single tracked root .pi-todos.json snapshot.
decisions.basis: A single structured file provides clone portability and Git review without a database, ignored .pi directory changes, or per-item file clutter.

decisions.text: Keep unscoped behavior session-oriented except when an active focused initiative owns the automatic execution view; require explicit project scope for durable mutations.
decisions.basis: This preserves compatibility and prevents incidental model decomposition from silently becoming durable repository state.

decisions.text: Do not synchronize, promote, or duplicate items across authorities.
decisions.basis: Authority isolation avoids partial cross-store transactions and duplicate lifecycle state.

risks.text: Concurrent Pi sessions could overwrite project todo changes.
risks.mitigation: Use cooperative locking, revision/hash compare-and-swap, atomic rename, directory sync, and concurrency tests.

risks.text: Adding a third provider could make default routing or mutation targets ambiguous.
risks.mitigation: Require explicit project scope, use authority-specific IDs and labels, recompute provider selection per operation, and reject scope/ID mismatches.

risks.text: A malformed or replaced .pi-todos.json file could be silently reset or followed through a symlink.
risks.mitigation: Use a closed bounded schema, stable path checks, regular non-symlink validation, and fail-closed diagnostics without fallback writes.

risks.text: A tracked todo file can create Git conflicts or unrelated commit noise.
risks.mitigation: Use collision-resistant IDs and deterministic serialization, never auto-commit, and document that normal scoped Git practices apply.

risks.text: Refactoring shared todo rules could regress session fork behavior or initiative gates.
risks.mitigation: Preserve current characterization tests, add authority-isolation tests, and run focused plus full qualification.
